scope: isolated W70 audit and candidate repair for actual helper offline part/element planning and aggregate batch completion copy

changes: offlinePartAsk now returns an empty queue and a truthful no-change clarification if any requested part cannot be selected, rather than leaving earlier valid part operations queued while claiming all requested parts were completed.
offlineElementAsk applies the same all-or-nothing compile refusal when any requested element is unavailable.
finishCore replaces the full-success sentence with explicit successful lines and failed operations when a real apply batch partially succeeds.

regression.baseline: 12/12 characterization assertions passed; two offline planner cases reproduce queued partial changes with false full-success copy, and forced apply failure reproduces stale full-success copy
regression.coverage: Actual extracted makeTools/offlinePartAsk/offlineElementAsk/applyQueue/finishCore with actual ZoneKit source in a VM; single/multi success; invalid and duplicate targets; malformed add; rejected edit; missing region; offline zero-mask/absent-element failures; forced addZone failure; existing-zone non-mutation on planner refusal. No browser, native painting, provider, network, or server calls.

findings_and_limits: Reachable offline part route gap: the planner accumulates selector errors but previously continued with valid operations and summarized all requested parts as completed. A synthetic template with a recognized right-side island but zero current pixels reproduced this through actual production functions. The candidate now refuses the whole compile result before any zone change.

Reachable offline element route gap: the planner previously queued found elements and omitted missing-element errors from its success sentence. A stripes-present/sponsors-absent fixture reproduced it; the candidate refuses the whole plan before mutation.

Actual ZoneKit batch applies operations sequentially and reports each failure; it does not roll back successful prior operations. A deliberate second addZone exception demonstrated partial commit and confirmed the prior finishCore copy retained a contradictory full-success claim. Candidate copy now names applied lines and failed operations. The thrown addZone failure was injected and is not evidence that ordinary validated route input naturally causes this failure.

Actual MCP makeTools handlers validate each operation before enqueueing. Invalid later edits, malformed adds, and ambiguous duplicate IDs are rejected before they enter the queue; prior valid operations remain queued. The model/provider may decide how to narrate that tool error, but no provider was called and provider-authored copy behavior is outside this audit.

No general rollback framework was added. Candidate covers the two concrete offline compile routes and makes apply-time partial results explicit; other asynchronous/external side effects are outside the isolated lane.
